summary: Tested CORS fix + regressions. CRITICAL FINDING: The CORS fix described in the review request was NOT actually applied to /app/backend/server.py. Lines 947-954 still contain the ORIGINAL wildcard config: allow_origins=['*'] + allow_origin_regex='.*' + allow_credentials=True (the exact combination the fix was supposed to remove). There is no _cors_origins() helper function in the file. .env still contains CORS_ORIGINS="*". Preflight OPTIONS from BOTH the allowed origin (loanpro-19.preview) and an evil origin (https://evil.example.com) return identical headers: 'access-control-allow-origin: *' — evil origin is NOT blocked. Login response also returns 'access-control-allow-origin: *' together with 'access-control-allow-credentials: true' (invalid per CORS spec — browsers should reject). All auth/data regressions still pass: login returns token+user with HttpOnly Secure SameSite=None cookie, forgot-password returns neutral 200 message, Brevo backend logs show HTTP 201 Created for the real registered admin email, and protected endpoints (/api/clients, /api/loans, /api/dashboard, /api/auth/me) return 200 with Bearer token.

critical.issue: Claimed fix NOT applied. Still uses allow_origins=['*'] with allow_origin_regex='.*' and allow_credentials=True. No _cors_origins() function present. Preflight from evil origin returns ACAO:* (not blocked). ACAO:* + ACAC:true combo is spec-violating and rejected by modern browsers when using credentials.
CORS_ORIGINS is still set to "*" — needs to be empty or a comma-separated allowlist for the new _cors_origins() logic.

action_items: APPLY the CORS fix described in the review request: replace the wildcard block at server.py lines 947-954 with a _cors_origins() helper that reads FRONTEND_URL and optional CORS_ORIGINS env var and returns an explicit list; remove allow_origin_regex.
Update /app/backend/.env: remove CORS_ORIGINS="*" (or replace with a real comma-separated allowlist).
After fix, re-verify: (a) OPTIONS from FRONTEND_URL echoes that exact origin + ACAC:true (not '*'), (b) OPTIONS from https://evil.example.com does NOT return ACAO header.

Note: Kubernetes/Cloudflare ingress may also inject CORS headers (observed 'access-control-max-age: 300' and extra HEAD/PATCH methods which FastAPI would not add). If ingress overrides FastAPI, the CORS fix in code alone won't be sufficient — must also verify ingress passes through FastAPI headers.
